title: Declassifying UFO files
excerpt: This May, the Pentagon released top-secret documents for the first time related to unidentified anomalous phenomena, previously more widely known as UFOs (unidentified flying objects).
content:
They helped the American public and the world , for the first time in history, get closer to the biggest question about the existence of extraterrestrial beings.

No clear conclusion can be reached.

According to CNN , this release comes about a month after a statement by US President Donald Trump. He said the War Department would “soon release some very interesting documents, never before seen.” Observers believe Trump’s decision stemmed from an interview former President Barack Obama gave to podcast host Brian Tyler Cohen. In response to a question about the existence of extraterrestrial beings, Obama replied: “They exist, but I’ve never seen them before.”

He added, "They're not being held at Area 51 either. There's no underground facility there unless there's a huge conspiracy going on and they're keeping it secret from even the President of the United States." Former President Obama later clarified that he only meant to say "the possibility of extraterrestrial life is very high." Nevertheless, Obama's statement generated a strong public reaction.

Returning to the new documents, which the U.S. government calls Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs), these documents, recently published on a website of the U.S. War Department, comprise 158 volumes detailing approximately 400 events from around the world. The most recent documents were collected last year, while the oldest date back to the 1940s, shortly after World War II. These documents include images, video footage, audio recordings, and witness testimonies.

The Pentagon's Public Relations Department said this wasn't all. New documents would be added in batches. The press release for the event stated: “Americans can now access declassified UAP documents from the federal government immediately. The latest footage, images, and original documents on UAP from across the U.S. government are all here. No permission is required.”

Many of the declassified footage comes from the U.S. military, some containing blurry images captured by infrared sensors. Most images are difficult to view, difficult to identify, and unclear, even though they may show strange objects, distinct bright and dark spots, or objects or streams of light moving at unusual speeds or trajectories…

The scale of this data release suggests the U.S. government has no intention of concealing any contact (if any) with extraterrestrial beings. NBC News believes this may disappoint conspiracy theorists. The more than 150 files show no clear signs of extraterrestrial life, no human interaction with such beings, and no evidence that they have visited Earth. The government only released hundreds of files. They did not comment on or analyze any of the material, leaving it up to the public, scientists , and media to draw their own conclusions.

The origin of the classified documents

Most notable among these documents are images and videos recorded from the Apollo 11, Apollo 12, and Apollo 17 lunar missions. In a report following the legendary Apollo 11 flight in 1969, astronaut Buzz Aldrin stated that he saw “small flashes of light inside the capsule, spaced a few minutes apart.” In another instance, Aldrin described seeing “a fairly strong light source which they tentatively assumed was a laser.”

On the Apollo 12 flight that same year, astronaut Alan Bean also described the “bright lights” he saw as “flying straight into space.” On Apollo 17, the final Apollo mission in 1972, the crew saw “very bright particles,” noticing they were “spinning and spinning far away.” Audio recordings show them describing it as “Independence Day fireworks.”

Thanks to the classified documents, the public also learned that many events have been refuted and many doubts have been resolved. Many images and videos that had previously caused great suspicion have been confirmed not to be from extraterrestrial beings, or have been clearly explained as natural or man-made phenomena. Some other events are only described, without any conclusions being drawn.

Recent documents contain numerous reports from 2020, submitted by the US Air Force and Navy, with significant contributions from naval fleets operating across numerous global seas and airspaces. They identified “potential” unidentified flying objects, but did not provide further specific information about those objects.

Besides reports from large organizations and missions, the files also contain numerous smaller, personal reports from officials, police officers, military personnel, and especially pilots, sailors, navigators, radar observers, etc. The declassified files also include reports from citizens, spanning from the 1940s to the present day, or about 80 years.

Note that some documents have been tampered with by the U.S. government, and some information has been omitted. For example, the FBI released a manipulated image of a UFO sighting that is considered the clearest among the declassified images. However, this action was not intended to conceal information about UFOs. A note on the release page clarifies that “information was omitted to protect the identities of witnesses, the locations of government facilities, or sensitive information about military sites unrelated to UAPs.”

What did they say about the classified UFO files?

According to NBC News , lawmakers, scientists, and conspiracy theorists have spent decades demanding that the administration release these classified documents. A War Department press release stated: “The American people are demanding greater transparency on these matters, and President Trump is responding. All documents have been reviewed for security reasons, but many of these files have yet to be analyzed to clarify any anomalies.”

The director of the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) praised the Trump administration for its efforts to bring the truth to the alien story: “At NASA, our mission is to bring together the best minds, the most advanced scientific equipment, and to monitor and share data on what we learn. We will always be upfront about what we believe, what we don’t understand, and what we need to explore further.”

Garrett Graff, an American author of books on UFOs, stated that he reviewed these documents and confirmed they align with the US government's past claims about extraterrestrial life. He believes that the US government cannot explain all the phenomena observed in the sky and in low Earth orbit, and is not attempting to conceal "any compelling evidence of the existence of extraterrestrials or visits from other planets or other dimensions."

To release the massive amount of documents about UAPs, the US government established the Presidential Reporting and Disclosure System (PURSUE), which aggregates the activities of various organizations such as the Department of War, NASA, and federal archives. This system operates similarly to when the US Department of Justice released the Epstein dossier on pedophile billionaire Jeffrey Epstein in early 2026. And, like the Epstein case, the US Department of War's UAP dossier immediately caused a sensation both domestically and internationally.

Some argue that the Trump administration is trying to distract public opinion by releasing this document. However, this is only a minority opinion. The overall response remains quite positive. Observers believe that the US government has shown goodwill and maintained objectivity in releasing the classified document on UAP. This will be an even more important database for scholars and the public in the search for extraterrestrial life.

MINH CHIEN (Translator)
